chunks: From him, from Muhammad, from Yunus, from Aban, from Abu Shaybah, who said:
I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) saying:
The knowledge of Ibn Shubrumah is astray in comparison with al-Jāmiʿah, dictated by the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) and written by ʿAlī (عليه السلام) with his own hand.
Indeed, al-Jāmiʿah has left no room for anyone's speech; in it is the knowledge of the halal (permissible) and the haram (forbidden).
Indeed, the companions of qiyās sought knowledge through analogy, but they increased in nothing from the truth except distance. Indeed, the religion of Allah cannot be attained through qiyās.

key_terms.إِمْلَاءِ: Dictation; here it refers to the direct dictation of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.
key_terms.الْجَامِعَةِ: The comprehensive written source dictated by the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and written by Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام.
key_terms.الْحَرَامِ: That which is forbidden in the Sacred Law.
key_terms.الْحَقِّ: The truth, from which reliance on qiyās causes one to become more distant.
key_terms.الْحَلَالِ: That which is permissible in the Sacred Law.
key_terms.الْقِيَاسِ: Analogical reasoning used to derive rulings, rejected here as a means to attain religious truth.
key_terms.خَطِّ: Handwriting; here it indicates that Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام physically wrote the text.
key_terms.دِينِ: The religion of Allah, which cannot be attained through qiyās.

ai.seo_question: Why does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام reject qiyās in understanding the religion of Allah?
ai.summary: This hadith affirms the authority of al-Jāmiʿah, the written corpus dictated by the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and inscribed by Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام, as a comprehensive source of knowledge concerning halal and haram. It rejects qiyās as a valid means of attaining the religion of Allah, stating that reliance on analogy only increases distance from the truth.

en.hubeali: From him, from Muhammad, from Yunus, from Aban, from Abu Shayba who said,
‘The knowledge of Ibn Shubrama (a judge) is a straying in the presence of Al-Jami’e (a book) dictated by Rasool-Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and written by Ali<sup>asws</sup> by his<sup>asws</sup> hand.
Al Jami’e has not left any speech (to be spoken) by anyone. In it is knowledge of the Permissible and the Prohibitions.

The companions of analogy are seeking the knowledge by the analogies, so it would not be increasing them from the Truth, except for the distance (from it). The Religion of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> cannot be attained by the analogy’.
en.sarwar: 14. It is narrated from him from Muhammad from Yunus from Aban from abu Shaybah who has said the following.
‘Ibn Shabrama’s knowledge is lost and void before al-Jami‘ah. It is a large book that was dictated by the holy Prophet to Imam Ali (a.s.), who wrote it with his own hands.
Al-Jami‘ah has left nothing for any one to say. In it is the knowledge of all lawful and unlawful matters.
The people of analogy sought knowledge through analogy and it increased to their knowledge but taking them away from knowledge. The religion of Allah is not of matters to learn through analogy.”
